## C-8.8 — Consent, as a matter of reporting and scope.

> Consent, as a matter of reporting and scope. CONFIRMED as an absence. The study reports approval by a named university ethics committee under a protocol code and compliance with the Declaration of Helsinki, and written informed consent from parents or legal guardians "for the administration of the assessment instruments". Verified absent from the full text: any mention of child assent; any data-protection, data-sharing or retention statement; any disclosure-control statement; and any operational definition of "anonymized". The repository record carries no ethics, consent or restriction statement. We frame this as a reporting-and-scope issue rather than a procedural failure: the consent quoted is scoped to being measured, and no statement in the published record establishes that it extends to open, unrestricted, perpetual republication of individual-level records on minors. Absence of a statement is not proof that broader consent was not obtained; what is confirmed is that the published record does not establish it.

- **Where in the comment:** Section 8
- **Found by:** A5
- **Settled in adjudication:** `A6` — Consent — A5, CONFIRMED from the paper and the Zenodo record
- **Figures asserted:** `8.8`

Absences in documents that are not in pkg/ cannot be checked from pkg/. A verifier confirms them by full-text search of the article and by opening the repository record.")

## C-A3 — Data-quality defects a replicator meets immediately.

> Data-quality defects a replicator meets immediately. Ten columns mix strings into numeric data — including "Did not want", "Ht or wt error" and "Age error", which are the only documentation in the entire deposit — and a naive read silently coerces the whole column to text. The values 99 and 88 are used as undocumented missing codes inside numeric anthropometric columns. Height is in centimetres in waves 1 and 2 and in metres in waves 3 and 4 under the same header, and one wave-4 height is zero. One instrument changes from a seven-point to a five-point response scale between waves 2 and 3 under the same header. Twenty-three Likert sum scores fall below their own arithmetic minimum. Sixteen height decreases appear across consecutive waves, four of them of 6 to 15 cm and physically impossible, alongside four weight losses of 11 to 26 kg; a further 41 apparent growth anomalies resolve benignly once one notices that school 1's first wave was collected a full academic year before the other four schools'. Three wave-4 columns have zero variance, and seventeen wave-4 columns are school-level values replicated down child rows, so their effective sample size is 5 rather than 483 — a live hazard for anyone extending the analysis to environmental determinants, though the paper analyses wave 3 and none of this touches a published number.

- **Where in the comment:** Appendix A
- **Found by:** A5
- **Settled in adjudication:** `A0` — Structural correction to my brief — A5, CONFIRMED
- **Figures asserted:** `99`, `88`, `15`, `11`, `26`, `41`, `483`

```{r C_A3}
## Data-quality defects a replicator meets immediately. Several are checked; three are marked.

       note = "tolerance 2: whether the identifier column and the class-letter columns count as 'numeric data contaminated by strings' is a boundary the comment does not draw")
expect("C-A3",
       anthropometric_columns_using_99_or_88 = 1,
       height_unit_changes_between_waves     = 1,
       wave4_heights_equal_to_zero           = 1,
       wave4_zero_variance_columns           = 3)
expect("C-A3", tol = 3, wave4_school_level_columns = 17)

mixed <- vapply(seq_len(NC), function(j) {
  x <- DAT[[j]]; x <- x[!is.na(x) & nzchar(trimws(x))]
  if (!length(x)) return(0L)
  as.integer(any(is.na(suppressWarnings(as.numeric(x))))) }, integer(1))
mostly_text <- vapply(seq_len(NC), function(j) {
  x <- DAT[[j]]; x <- x[!is.na(x) & nzchar(trimws(x))]
  if (!length(x)) return(0L)
  as.integer(mean(is.na(suppressWarnings(as.numeric(x)))) >= 0.5) }, integer(1))

codes <- as.integer(any(vapply(c(W3$weight, W3$height, W3$c21, W3$c9_1, W3$c9_2), function(j)
  any(NUM[, j] %in% c(88, 99), na.rm = TRUE), logical(1))))
hh <- vapply(BLOCK, function(b) median(NUM[, b[HDR[b] == "8"]], na.rm = TRUE), numeric(1))
h4 <- NUM[, BLOCK$w4[HDR[BLOCK$w4] == "8"]]
zv <- vapply(BLOCK$w4, function(j) {
  x <- NUM[, j]; x <- x[!is.na(x)]
  as.integer(length(x) > 50 && sd(x) == 0) }, integer(1))
sl <- vapply(BLOCK$w4, function(j) {
  x <- NUM[, j]; k <- !is.na(x) & !is.na(SCHOOL)
  if (sum(k) < 50) return(0L)
  as.integer(all(tapply(x[k], SCHOOL[k], function(v) length(unique(v)) == 1))) }, integer(1))

check("C-A3", columns_mixing_strings_into_numbers = sum(mixed) - sum(mostly_text))
check("C-A3",
      anthropometric_columns_using_99_or_88 = codes,
      height_unit_changes_between_waves     = as.integer(any(hh > 3) && any(hh < 3)),
      wave4_heights_equal_to_zero           = sum(h4 == 0, na.rm = TRUE),
      wave4_zero_variance_columns           = sum(zv))
check("C-A3", wave4_school_level_columns = sum(sl))

unverifiable("C-A3",
  "Three clauses of this paragraph are not checked here: the 23 Likert sums below their own arithmetic minimum and the 16 height decreases across consecutive waves both require the per-instrument item counts and the wave alignment the audit reconstructed by hand, and the response-scale change from seven to five points between waves 2 and 3 requires knowing which header is the same instrument across waves. None changes a published number and the comment says so.")
```

## C-A4 — One identity that does not close.

> One identity that does not close. In waves 3 and 4 the stored subscale mean does not equal the stored sum divided by its item count on roughly 1 to 3 percent of rows. This is not rounding — the hypothesis that the mean equals the sum over the item count rounded to two decimals explains none of them — and deviations reach 3.0 points on a five-point scale, so the stored mean and the stored sum describe different response sets. Since the published trees split on the *means*, a small number of children are placed by a value that contradicts the raw score beside it. The raw questionnaire items are not deposited, so this cannot be repaired from the file.

- **Where in the comment:** Appendix A
- **Found by:** A2
- **Settled in adjudication:** `A13` — The variable dictionary was recovered from arithmetic alone — A2, strong positive
- **Figures asserted:** `3 percent`, `3.0`

```{r C_A4}
## The one identity that does not close: the stored subscale mean is not the stored sum over its
## item count on 1-3 per cent of wave-3 and wave-4 rows, and it is not rounding.
##
## The sum/mean pairs are discovered rather than hard-coded: adjacent columns whose ratio has a
## stable integer median are a sum and its mean, and the integer is the item count.
expect("C-A4", tol = 0.6, worst_pair_mismatch_rate_pct = 3.0,
       note = "the comment says 'roughly 1 to 3 percent of rows'")
expect("C-A4", tol = 0.5, largest_deviation_scale_points = 3.0)
expect("C-A4", explained_by_two_decimal_rounding = 0, pairs_discovered_at_least = 1)

res <- list()
for (w in c(3, 4)) for (j in BLOCK[[w]]) {
  if (j + 1 > max(BLOCK[[w]])) next
  s <- NUM[, j]; m <- NUM[, j + 1]
  ok <- !is.na(s) & !is.na(m) & m != 0
  if (sum(ok) < 100) next
  r <- median(s[ok] / m[ok]); k <- round(r)
  if (k < 2 || k > 40 || abs(r - k) > 0.02) next
  bad <- abs(s / k - m) > 1e-9 & ok
  if (sum(bad) / sum(ok) > 0.2) next          # not a sum/mean pair, just a correlated pair
  rnd <- abs(round(s / k, 2) - m) < 1e-9 & ok
  res[[length(res) + 1]] <- data.frame(
    wave = w, sum_col = j, mean_col = j + 1, header = HDR[j], k = k,
    n = sum(ok), bad = sum(bad), pct = 100 * sum(bad) / sum(ok),
    rounding = sum(bad & rnd),
    worst = if (any(bad)) max(abs((s / k - m)[bad])) else 0)
}
res <- do.call(rbind, res)
print(res[res$bad > 0, ], row.names = FALSE, digits = 3)
cat(sprintf("pairs discovered: %d; overall mismatch %d of %d rows (%.1f%%)\n",
            nrow(res), sum(res$bad), sum(res$n), 100 * sum(res$bad) / sum(res$n)))

check("C-A4", worst_pair_mismatch_rate_pct = round(max(res$pct), 1))
check("C-A4", largest_deviation_scale_points = round(max(res$worst), 1))
check("C-A4",
      explained_by_two_decimal_rounding = sum(res$rounding),
      pairs_discovered_at_least         = as.integer(nrow(res) >= 20))
```

## C-ABS.2 — The undocumented file is largely recoverable: we identify 24 of about 30 reported variabl...

> The undocumented file is largely recoverable: we identify 24 of about 30 reported variables, mostly by exact arithmetic identity; the analytic sample recovers to within one participant; every aggregate identity in the file reproduces with zero violations; the published tree figure's internal arithmetic is flawless; and the paper's central claim survives, with cardiovascular endurance the root split in 90 to 97 percent of bootstrap resamples.

- **Where in the comment:** Abstract
- **Found by:** A1
- **Settled in adjudication:** `A17` — Negative results that must be prominent — A1
- **Figures asserted:** `24`, `30`, `90`, `97 percent`

```{r C_ABS_2}
## The abstract's positive-results sentence, checked clause by clause against the body results
## this notebook has already produced. An abstract figure that is not the body figure is the
## failure mode this cross-reference exists to catch.
expect("C-ABS.2",
       sample_gap                = 1,
       aggregate_identity_violations = 0,
       tree_figure_exceptions    = 0)
expect("C-ABS.2", tol = 5,
       boot_root_low_end_pct = 90, boot_root_high_end_pct = 97,
       note = "the abstract's '90 to 97 percent' band; tolerance as in C-2.11, this is Monte Carlo")

check("C-ABS.2",
      sample_gap = observed_of("C-2.5", "gap_vs_paper"),
      aggregate_identity_violations =
        observed_of("C-2.7", "subscale_sum_violations") + observed_of("C-2.7", "rai_violations"),
      tree_figure_exceptions =
        observed_of("C-2.9", "parent_child_mismatches") +
        observed_of("C-2.9", "row_sum_mismatches") +
        observed_of("C-2.9", "purity_rule_exceptions"))
check("C-ABS.2",
      boot_root_low_end_pct  = min(observed_of("C-2.11", "boot_root_pct_balanced"),
                                   observed_of("C-2.11", "boot_root_pct_default")),
      boot_root_high_end_pct = max(observed_of("C-2.11", "boot_root_pct_balanced"),
                                   observed_of("C-2.11", "boot_root_pct_default")))

judgement("C-ABS.2",
  "The abstract's '24 of about 30 reported variables' is the classification judgement of C-2.4, carried into the abstract unchanged.",
  "Checked there, not here. Recorded so that the abstract sentence is not counted as verified arithmetic when part of it is not arithmetic at all.")
```

## Summary

```{r summary, error=TRUE}
STUB_CLAIMS <- c()
declared <- .V$order
rows <- do.call(rbind, lapply(declared, function(key) {
  e <- .V$exp[[key]]; o <- .V$obs[[key]]
  if (is.null(e)) e <- list(id = strsplit(key, "\\|")[[1]][1],
                            key = strsplit(key, "\\|")[[1]][2], expected = NA, tol = NA)
  data.frame(claim = e$id, key = e$key,
             expected = .fmt(e$expected),
             observed = if (is.null(o)) "-- never computed --" else .fmt(o$observed),
             tol      = .fmt(e$tol),
             verdict  = if (is.null(o)) "FAIL" else o$verdict,
             detail   = if (is.null(o)) "expectation declared but no check() ran" else o$detail,
             stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
}))
states <- do.call(rbind, lapply(.V$state, function(s)
  data.frame(claim = s$id, key = "-", expected = "-", observed = "-", tol = "-",
             verdict = s$verdict, detail = s$detail, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)))
stubs <- if (length(STUB_CLAIMS))
  data.frame(claim = STUB_CLAIMS, key = "-", expected = "-", observed = "-", tol = "-",
             verdict = "FAIL", detail = "TODO stub: no check has been written for this claim",
             stringsAsFactors = FALSE) else NULL
all_rows <- rbind(rows, states, stubs)
all_rows <- all_rows[order(all_rows$claim, all_rows$key), ]

cat("\n"); cat(strrep("=", 100), "\n")
cat("VERIFICATION SUMMARY\n")
cat(strrep("=", 100), "\n")
print(knitr::kable(all_rows, row.names = FALSE))

n_pass <- sum(all_rows$verdict == "PASS")
n_fail <- sum(all_rows$verdict == "FAIL")
n_jud  <- sum(all_rows$verdict == "JUDGEMENT")
n_unv  <- sum(all_rows$verdict == "UNVERIFIABLE")
claims_covered <- length(unique(all_rows$claim))

cat("\n")
cat(sprintf("claims with at least one outcome : %d\n", claims_covered))
cat(sprintf("checks PASS                      : %d\n", n_pass))
cat(sprintf("checks FAIL                      : %d\n", n_fail))
cat(sprintf("claims marked JUDGEMENT          : %d\n", n_jud))
cat(sprintf("claims marked UNVERIFIABLE       : %d\n", n_unv))
cat(sprintf("claims still a TODO stub         : %d%s\n", length(STUB_CLAIMS),
            if (length(STUB_CLAIMS)) paste0("  <-- ", paste(STUB_CLAIMS, collapse = ", ")) else ""))

## the deposit must be untouched
after <- .pkg_manifest()
same <- identical(.PKG_ON_ENTRY[order(.PKG_ON_ENTRY$file), c("file", "size", "md5")],
                  after[order(after$file), c("file", "size", "md5")])
cat(sprintf("deposit unmodified               : %s\n", if (same) "yes" else "NO -- INVESTIGATE"))
if (!same) n_fail <- n_fail + 1

if (n_fail > 0) {
  cat("\n"); cat(strrep("!", 100), "\n")
  cat(sprintf("!!  VERIFICATION FAILED: %d check(s) did not reproduce\n", n_fail))
  bad <- all_rows[all_rows$verdict == "FAIL", ]
  for (i in seq_len(nrow(bad)))
    cat(sprintf("!!    %-12s %-22s expected %-18s observed %-18s %s\n",
                bad$claim[i], bad$key[i], bad$expected[i], bad$observed[i], bad$detail[i]))
  cat(strrep("!", 100), "\n")
} else {
  cat("\nAll declared checks reproduced.\n")
}

utils::write.csv(all_rows, "verification_summary.csv", row.names = FALSE)
writeLines(as.character(as.integer(n_fail > 0)), "verification_status.txt")
unlink(SCRATCH, recursive = TRUE)

if (n_fail > 0)
  stop(sprintf("verification failed: %d check(s) did not reproduce (see the table above)", n_fail))
```

The chunk above writes `verification_summary.csv` and `verification_status.txt` (`0` clean,
`1` if anything failed). To get a nonzero **process** exit as well:

```sh
Rscript -e 'rmarkdown::render("verification.Rmd"); \
           quit(status = as.integer(readLines("verification_status.txt")))'
```
